entries.summary: Renewed oil supply shock materially weakens Friday relief prospects and increases Monday downside risk; US cash response unobserved.
bullish: QQQ recovered 3.73 percentage points from morning observation.
Russell 2000 and Dow closed higher; reported 10Y yield fell.
Equal-weight RSP gained 0.78% while SPY fell 0.30% in a secondary closing report.
FT and WSJ report Asian technology-heavy markets rebounding Thursday; proposed tariffs may replace existing levies rather than stack.
IBD reports Nasdaq-100 futures +1.05% versus S&P futures +0.7% overnight; exact quote time unavailable.
IBD reports both NQ and ES futures up 0.55%; holiday relief persists.
FT reports ASML +2.5% and Stoxx 600 +1.5% Thursday, indicating overseas technology relief.
bearish: QQQ lagged SPY by 0.36 percentage points at close.
Reuters reports semiconductor and AI credit stress; VIX rose despite recovery.
SMH reportedly lost 8% over five sessions; secondary SOX report indicates severe weakness, exact timestamp unavailable.
Oil supply disruption risk is corroborated by Reuters; inflation sensitivity remains elevated.
Curated core PCE 3.3% versus 3.2% consensus and GDP 4.3% versus 3.6% forecast reinforce tightening risk; tariff proposals are not yet effective.
S&P CreditWatch Negative on Nvidia AA rating adds financing/governance risk; no downgrade or isolated price reaction confirmed.
IBD reports Micron down 4.5% Wednesday; latest reported NQ futures no longer outperform ES.
Reuters reports China reserves the right to respond to tariffs; Korean chipmakers pared early gains according to FT.
Reuters reports Brent $96.25 and WTI $84.78 after renewed reported Middle East supply disruptions; WSJ independently corroborates rising oil. Exact quote times unavailable.

editorial.marketOverview: Thanksgiving closes US cash equities. AP reports overseas gains and positive US futures, but Wednesday Nasdaq fell 0.6% and Nvidia 3.9%. These are historical or holiday observations, not a synchronized live panel. Prior dashboard yields and Fed settlement pricing remain carried forward, not refreshed.
editorial.whatChanged: Reuters now reports Brent $96.25 and WTI $84.78 after renewed reported refinery and shipping disruptions, versus earlier reported $93.79 and $83.33. WSJ corroborates direction at different levels. Exact observation times are unavailable, so the comparison is indicative rather than a measured synchronized return. Open Watch remains at 181 events.
editorial.marketInterpretation: The oil reversal adds inflation and discount-rate risk to already weak semiconductor leadership and hawkish prior Fed pricing. The observed oil response is distinct from expected Nasdaq impact: no US cash reaction is possible today. The earlier holiday futures bounce may predate the oil move. No new synchronized yields, SOX, VXN or Nasdaq breadth were verified.
editorial.threeDayPath: Friday: relief rally is more vulnerable to fading in the shortened session. Monday: normal liquidity and the weekend OPEC+ decision could amplify or reverse the oil risk premium. Tuesday: JOLTS and tentatively listed chip earnings could redirect the path. The three-session skew is now bearish, not a certainty.
editorial.bullCase: Oil retreats as supply fears ease, overseas technology strength translates into US semiconductor leadership, and QQQ holds Wednesday recovery with wider participation and lower volatility.
editorial.bearCase: Persistent oil strength compounds inflation risk and AI financing concerns, causing a failed Friday bounce and renewed selling Monday. Tariff retaliation would add risk. No isolated equity reaction to the new oil headlines has been established.
editorial.watchNext: Track oil with timestamped quotes, Friday QQQ/SOX relative performance, VXN/VIX, Nasdaq advance-decline, paired Treasury yields and Fed pricing. Monitor Sunday OPEC+ and Tuesday JOLTS; confirm issuer earnings dates.
